title: The Lesson I Learned From the Boy Who Gave His Lunch
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned From the Boy Who Gave His Lunch
John 6:9
There was a boy in the crowd.

Not famous.
Not powerful.
Not preaching.
Just carrying lunch.
“Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but how far will they go among so many?” — John 6:9
Read that again.

They saw “not enough.”
Jesus saw a miracle.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The miracle did not begin when the bread multiplied.
It began when the boy released what was in his hands.

You keep saying, “I don’t have enough.”
Enough faith.
Enough wisdom.
Enough strength.
Enough holiness.
Enough influence.
God saw it.
He saw the little you were hiding because you thought it was too small to matter.
You knew.
You knew Jesus was asking for surrender, but fear whispered, “What if He takes it and nothing happens?”
But the Gospel crushes that fear.

Because Jesus did not come for people who had enough.
He came for the empty, the weak, the sinful, the hungry.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That crowd was hungry.
But your deeper hunger is not bread.

It is forgiveness.
Mercy.
Rescue.
New life.
And Jesus is not merely the One who multiplies bread.
He is the Bread.
“I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me shall not hunger.” — John 6:35

The boy gave lunch.
Jesus gave Himself.

The boy surrendered bread.
Jesus surrendered His body.
At the cross, Christ took the little, broken, guilty offering of sinners and answered it with blood, grace, and resurrection power.
“By grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.” — Ephesians 2:8–9
So stop measuring your life by what you lack.
Bring it to Jesus.

Your broken obedience.
Your small faith.
Your tired prayers.
Your surrendered “yes.”
He can feed thousands with what you thought was worthless.

Repent.
Trust Christ.
Follow Him.
The lesson is this:

What stays in your hands remains small.
What is surrendered to Jesus becomes testimony.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
